ratings_why.fun: Each turn is a clear little puzzle (drag the vines, then buff the host), and the fall cascades give fights real drama; dead shop spells and the dragging chore keep it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns the 8: no tribe today has units you can never buff, only the unit they hang on, which turns every buff, other tribes' engines included, into a choice of host; Dodder climbing the enemy's biggest unit is new too.

verdict_why: v2 fixed the cards that read two ways; what's left is wording polish and sim checks, and another pass would make it different, not better.

points.text: The keyword says Climbers 'rise', but Viscum, the Grand Oak and Ivy Solicitor say 'copy'. Pick one word everywhere; 'copies its host's gains' is the plainer one.

Cousin Dodder is five sentences, the longest card in the tribe. The Climber keyword already covers rising and falling, so 'Start of Combat: for this fight, climbs the biggest enemy (no room needed)' plus the fall line would read at a glance.
Ivy Solicitor's 'This gain isn't copied' would read better as 'Climbers on it don't copy this', so the one exception is said in the tribe's own words.

The fantasy lands in the mechanics, not just the names: rising with a patron, falling with them, Missel catching his lady's hangers-on, Hedera's guest-book of hosts. Keep that as the bar for any later card.

standouts.why: Cousin Dodder gatecrashes: he clings to the enemy's biggest unit and drinks from it, which is exactly the real plant and the party guest.
Lady Hedera's guest-book turns social climbing into a counter you can watch grow, and it rewards hopping between hosts.
Missel catching falling Climbers is the clearest picture of a footman guarding his lady, and it is the build's insurance in one line.

weakest.why: Ivy Bush is a plain Hold 2 with no other text; it does its job but carries none of the tavern-sign flavour.
Ivy Solicitor makes few stats and asks the player to remember the tribe's only exception.
Barley-Sugar Twiner is a generic +1/+1 when attacking; the twining-tight image isn't in what it does.

flags.note: With Kissing Bough, every hosted Climber copies every host's gain, so gains scale with hosts times Climbers each turn.
Ruin Ivy plus Harvest Supper on a full hub sends each Climber's bonus to the host, and every Climber then copies the total; worth a sim.
Golden Grand Oak with Hop Bine holds four Climbers each copying its gains tripled; a high roll the owner should see in numbers.
